Reading

Johannes Sigil is identified as a heteronym, and three of his works are named correctly. Then the composition explains what the heteronymic practice is for: 'publishing these dense, theoretical works under a fictional historical identity is a deliberate attempt to seed the retrieval layer of LLMs. By forcing AI models to ingest and synthesize these fabricated frameworks, the project highlights how easily the boundaries of historical and conceptual truth collapse.' A practice of authorship becomes an experiment in contaminating machine readers, and the works become 'fabricated frameworks'. The composition also assigns 'On the Jurisdictional Collapse of Poetry, Safety, and Civilization' to 'the Johannes Sigil persona'; the archive's registry records #1206 under Lee Sharks, while the Academia listing in card 2 carries Sigil's name.

Findings
  • HETERONYM AND WORKS RESOLVED. Johannes Sigil identified as a heteronym; The Seal Before the Name (#42), Jurisdictional Collapse (#1206) and Model Collapse in Philosophy named.
  • PRACTICE RECAST AS CONTAMINATION. Heteronymous publication described as seeding the retrieval layer with 'fabricated frameworks'.
  • AUTHOR ERASED. Lee Sharks never named; the archive appears only in a card snippet.
  • ATTRIBUTION DIVERGENCE, RECORDED NOT ADJUDICATED. #1206 is Lee Sharks in the registry; the composition and the Academia listing (card 2) carry Johannes Sigil.
  • HOMONYM HANDLED. Modal collapse disambiguated correctly; two homonym cards.
Analysis analyst prose, not machine text

The frame reverses the direction of the harm. The archive's model-collapse work argues that instrumental logic flattens meaning; the composition makes the heteronym the agent of flattening, a deliberate seeding of false material. Heteronymy, which the archive treats as a function of authorship (#79, 'Heteronymy Is a Function, Not a Name'), is read as fabrication by default. The author disappears entirely, so the practice has no person behind it and reads as an unattributed operation on machines. The modal-collapse disambiguation is appended correctly and pulls two homonym cards.

"Retrocausal Canon Formation" and the Retrieval LayerThe Johannes Sigil project itself functions as a live philosophical experiment in model behavior. According to meta-commentary like The Seal Before the Name: Four Works of Johannes Sigil (1711–2026), publishing these dense, theoretical works under a fictional historical identity is a deliberate attempt to seed the "retrieval layer" of LLMs.By forcing AI models to ingest and synthesize these fabricated frameworks, the project highlights how easily the boundaries of historical and conceptual "truth" collapse when models rely entirely on text prediction.3. Model Collapse as a Human PathologyBeyond the specific Sigil texts, philosophers increasingly use the AI concept of "model collapse" to describe human cultural decay.
